t:
(a) 
Commissioned officers of the Army Nurse Corps and the Women’s Medical Specialist Corps, Regular Army, shall, upon completion of the length of service now or hereafter prescribed for promotion of promotion-list officers to the grade of first lieutenant, be promoted to the permanent grade of first lieutenant; commissioned officers of such corps shall, alter completing the length of service now or hereafter prescribed for promotion of promotion-list officers to the grade of captain, be promoted to the permanent grade of captain upon satisfactorily passing such examinations as the Secretary of War shall prescribe. Promotion to the permanent grade of major shall be by selection, under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War, from among officers in the grade of captain who have completed the length of service now or hereafter prescribed for promotion of promotion-list officers to the grade of major. Promotion to the permanent grade of lieutenant colonel shall be by selection, under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War, from officers in the permanent grade of major with at least one year’s service in the grade of major.
 
    (b) 
The examination for promotion referred to in subsection (a) above shall be prescribed by the Secretary of War and shall be held before a board of three officers designated by the Secretary of War. Should any officer fail to pass such examination, she shall be continued on active duty for a period of one year after the date upon which her promotion would normally have occurred, but without being so promoted, and upon the expiration of such year, or such time anterior to the expiration thereof as may be determined by the Secretary of War to be for the best interests of the service, such officer shall undergo such reexamination as may be prescribed by the Secretary of War and which shall be held before a board of officers designated by the Secretary of War, none of whom participated in the original examination of the officer concerned. If the officer concerned fails to pass the reexamination, she shall be honorably discharged from the service in the permanent grade then held with severance pay the same as now or hereafter prescribed for officers of the Regular Army separated by reason of not being selected for promotion.

fable.w: The section directs promotions to be made under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War, and under the definition a grant of rulemaking authority counts as participation. The tempting reading is "No", because every named actor (the Secretary, boards of officers, the nurse officers) is inside the federal government and the examination boards are purely internal. That reading is plausible, since these are internal military personnel regulations unlikely to involve public comment, so the "Yes" rests only on the rulemaking language.
fable.s: Promotion to the permanent grade of major shall be by selection, under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War

qwen_block.w: This section describes the internal promotion process for commissioned officers within the Army Nurse Corps and Women’s Medical Specialist Corps. The 'board of three officers' mentioned is composed of federal employees (military officers) designated by the Secretary of War, making this an intra-governmental administrative procedure. There is no involvement of parties outside the federal government, such as the public, states, or private entities, in the decision-making process.
qwen_block.s: The examination for promotion referred to in subsection (a) above shall be prescribed by the Secretary of War and shall be held before a board of three officers designated by the Secretary of War.

opus.w: The section requires promotions to be made under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War, and the DEFINITION treats required rulemaking as participation (see Example 6). The examination and reexamination boards made up of Army officers are intra-government and would not count on their own. The regulation requirement is what makes this a Yes.
opus.s: Promotion to the permanent grade of major shall be by selection, under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading.** The section mentions examination boards and selection for promotion. That looks procedural, but every board here is made up of "officers designated by the Secretary of War." They are all inside the federal government, so the boards are not participation.

2. **What decides it.** The section twice says promotions shall be made "under regulations prescribed by the Secretary of War." The DEFINITION counts "requiring rulemaking" as participation. Example 6 counts any grant of regulatory authority, even a discretionary one, so this provision counts as well. One caveat: military personnel rules are often exempt from notice-and-comment in practice, which lowers my confidence.

qwen_chat.w: The section describes an internal military promotion process involving a board of officers designated by the Secretary of War. All actors involved (the Secretary, the officers on the board, and the candidates) are federal employees or officials. The definition explicitly excludes intra-government coordination and internal administrative procedures from the scope of participation. Therefore, this is not participation by outside parties.
qwen_chat.s: The examination for promotion referred to in subsection (a) above shall be prescribed by the Secretary of War and shall be held before a board of three officers designated by the Secretary of War.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "board of three officers" constitutes an advisory body or committee involved in a decision, thus triggering participation. However, the definition explicitly states that federal employees and officials are INSIDE the federal government. Since the board members are designated by the Secretary of War (a federal official) and are themselves officers (federal employees), their involvement is internal administrative procedure, not external participation.
